Distrust people? Oh, no, not at all. I've always been a very trusting person. Too trusting, maybe. I used to be the one at the office who would leave my purse right out on my desk when I went to the restroom. I mean, we're all adults, right? She had on this little red velvet dress with white tights that got a chocolate stain on them before we even made it to the line... but, anyway, no, I don't hear people talking when nobody is there. Just regular house noises.\n\nDoctor: Have there been times when you felt unusually high, energetic, or full of energy for days at a time?\n\nPatient: Unusually high or energetic? No, I don't think so. I've always been pretty steady. I mean, I have to be, with my job. Working as a billing clerk, you sit a lot. You really have to make sure you get up and stretch, otherwise your lower back just completely locks up. My sister-in-law, the one who married my brother David, she bought me one of those ergonomic cushions for my desk chair last Christmas. It’s got this memory foam in it that's supposed to mold to your shape. She got it off one of those home shopping channels, I think. She watches QVC all day long, buying the most ridiculous things. Last month she bought this set of copper pots that she swore were non-stick, but the very first time she tried to make scrambled eggs, they stuck right to the bottom. It took her three days of soaking just to get it clean. But anyway, no, I haven't had any days where I felt like I was full of energy or anything like that. Just my normal routine.\n\nDoctor: If someone shows you clear proof that your husband’s family is not involved, are you able to accept that?\n\nPatient: Clear proof? Well... what kind of proof are we talking about? Because I've seen the records they pull up, and I know how easy it is to doctor a spreadsheet or a bank statement. People think computers are foolproof, but they aren't. My nephew, the one who just started his freshman year at State—he's studying computer science, actually. He built his own computer in his bedroom from parts he ordered online. It took up his whole desk, and it had these glowing blue lights inside the case. His mother was furious because he spent his entire summer job savings on it instead of saving for a car. She drives this old Honda Civic that’s been making a terrible rattling noise under the hood, but she refuses to take it to the mechanic because she says they always try to upsell her on air filters and wiper blades... \n\nBut anyway, what I'm saying is, I wouldn't believe their \"proof.\" I know what I know. For months I've been trying to get people to understand that his family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. The billing errors at work, the way the ladies at church are suddenly acting so funny toward me... no matter what piece of paper someone tries to show me, I know it all ties back to them. They're doing it, and I'm not going to just pretend they aren't because someone hands me a fake printout.\n\nDoctor: Do people ever tell you that your thoughts or the way you talk jump around or are hard to follow?\n\nPatient: Jump around? No, nobody's ever said that to me. I think I'm pretty clear when I speak. You have to be clear when you work in billing. If you get one number wrong, or explain a code poorly, the whole insurance claim gets kicked back. And you know how insurance companies are. They'll use any excuse to deny a claim. My cousin Brenda, she had this terrible time with her insurance last year when she needed that knee surgery. She tore her meniscus slipping on the ice in her driveway. It was one of those freak ice storms we got in February, remember? The whole city basically shut down for two days. The salt trucks didn't even make it to her neighborhood until the second afternoon. She was trying to walk down to get the mail because she was waiting for a birthday card from her son who lives out in Arizona. He moved out there for the dry heat, says it helps his allergies. But anyway, no, people don't tell me I'm hard to follow. I just tell things exactly how they happen.\n\nDoctor: Have you found yourself losing interest in seeing people or doing things you usually enjoy?\n\nPatient: Losing interest? No, I don't think so. I mean, I still like doing the things I usually do. Like my garden, I try to keep up with the flower beds out front. Mostly marigolds and some petunias. Though I will say, the slugs have been absolutely terrible this year. Have you noticed that? It's because we had such a wet spring. My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, he's lived next door for thirty years, he told me to put out little shallow dishes of beer to catch them. He says they're attracted to the yeast or something and they just crawl right in and drown. He buys the cheapest beer he can find at the discount liquor store over on 4th Street. The one next to that old dry cleaner that closed down? I used to take my winter coats there, but the last time I did, they lost the belt to my navy trench coat and refused to pay for it. The owner was this very stubborn man who insisted I brought it in without a belt. Why would I bring a trench coat in without a belt? It completely ruins the silhouette. The picture quality was terrible compared to what we have now, but we didn't know any better. We'd rent VHS tapes from Blockbuster on Friday nights. Remember Blockbuster? It's such a shame they all closed down. I used to love walking down the aisles, looking at all the covers. The smell of the popcorn they sold by the register... I bought a box of microwave popcorn last week, the extra butter kind, but it just doesn't taste the same. I think they changed the oil they use or something. The bag says \"new and improved flavor,\" but whenever a company says that, it usually just means they found a cheaper way to make it. It's like the brand of coffee I used to buy for the office breakroom. One day the packaging changed, and suddenly it tasted like burnt toast. I had to switch us to a different brand, which caused a whole fuss with the accounting department because it cost fifty cents more a can. But anyway, no, nobody can read my thoughts. I just keep them to myself, especially with everything his family is doing. You have to keep your thoughts private these days.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe your husband’s family has any special powers or unusual ways of controlling events that other people wouldn’t normally be able to do?\n\nPatient: Special powers? No, no, they don't have magic powers or anything like that. That's ridiculous. They're just very... manipulative. They know how to pull strings. Speaking of pulling strings, did you know I used to knit? I made this beautiful cable-knit sweater for my husband for our fifth anniversary. It took me months. I had to special order the yarn from a little shop up in Maine because I wanted this specific heather gray color. The woman who ran the shop, Mrs. Higgins, she was so sweet. She used to send a little handwritten note with every order and a complimentary stitch marker. They were always shaped like little sheep. I had quite a collection of them by the time she retired and closed the shop. It's so hard to find good quality wool these days without spending a fortune. Everything in the craft stores now is acrylic. It just doesn't breathe the same way, you know? You put on an acrylic sweater and five minutes later you're sweating, but you're still cold. It makes no sense. I tried to explain that to my sister when she started making baby blankets, but she just wanted something you could throw in the washer. But no, his family doesn't have special powers. They're just very good at getting people to do what they want, normal things, just... twisted.\n\nDoctor: Before all of this started, have you generally tended to distrust other people and suspect they were trying to harm or deceive you?\n\nPatient: Distrust people? Oh, no, not at all. I've always been a very trusting person. Too trusting, maybe. I used to be the one at the office who would leave my purse right out on my desk when I went to the restroom. I mean, we're all adults, right? We had this one woman, Brenda, who started in the billing department a few years ago. She was always borrowing things. A pen here, a stapler there. One time she borrowed my favorite mug—it was this ceramic one I got on a trip to Sedona, painted with these beautiful little desert flowers. The glaze was so vibrant. Anyway, she borrowed it for her tea and then left it in the sink for three days. I finally had to wash it myself. It's just that now, with his family, they've given me plenty of reasons. But before that? No, I never thought people were out to get me.\n\nDoctor: Have you been convinced that your husband’s family is doing this for more than one month?\n\nPatient: Oh, definitely more than a month. It's been going on for about nine months now. It all started right around the time we had that big blow-up over money and the holiday expectations. Holidays used to be so nice, you know? I used to bake these incredible gingerbread cookies from scratch. My grandmother gave me the recipe. My husband used to drink his coffee black, just like his father did. His father was a very stern man, never smiled in pictures. He built his own computer in his bedroom from parts he ordered online. It took up his whole desk, and it had these glowing blue lights inside the case. His mother was furious because he spent his entire summer job savings on it instead of saving for a car. No, nobody's ever said that to me. I think I'm pretty clear when I speak. You have to be clear when you work in billing. If you get one number wrong, or explain a code poorly, the whole insurance claim gets kicked back. And you know how insurance companies are. They'll use any excuse to deny a claim. My cousin Brenda, she had this terrible time with her insurance last year when she needed that knee surgery. She tore her meniscus slipping on the ice in her driveway. It was one of those freak ice storms we got in February, remember? The whole city basically shut down for two days. The salt trucks didn't even make it to her neighborhood until the second afternoon. She was trying to walk down to get the mail because she was waiting for a birthday card from her son who lives out in Arizona. He moved out there for the dry heat, says it helps his allergies. I had quite a collection of them by the time she retired and closed the shop. It's so hard to find good quality wool these days without spending a fortune. Everything in the craft stores now is acrylic. It just doesn't breathe the same way, you know? You put on an acrylic sweater and five minutes later you're sweating, but you're still cold. Just my normal routine.\n\nDoctor: If someone shows you clear proof that your husband’s family is not involved, are you able to accept that?\n\nPatient: Clear proof? Well... what kind of proof are we talking about? Because I've seen the records they pull up, and I know how easy it is to doctor a spreadsheet or a bank statement. People think computers are foolproof, but they aren't. My nephew, the one who just started his freshman year at State—he's studying computer science, actually. He built his own computer in his bedroom from parts he ordered online. It took up his whole desk, and it had these glowing blue lights inside the case. His mother was furious because he spent his entire summer job savings on it instead of saving for a car. She drives this old Honda Civic that’s been making a terrible rattling noise under the hood, but she refuses to take it to the mechanic because she says they always try to upsell her on air filters and wiper blades... \n\nBut anyway, what I'm saying is, I wouldn't believe their \"proof.\" I know what I know. For months I've been trying to get people to understand that his family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. The billing errors at work, the way the ladies at church are suddenly acting so funny toward me... no matter what piece of paper someone tries to show me, I know it all ties back to them. They're doing it, and I'm not going to just pretend they aren't because someone hands me a fake printout.\n\nDoctor: Do people ever tell you that your thoughts or the way you talk jump around or are hard to follow?\n\nPatient: Jump around? No, nobody's ever said that to me. I think I'm pretty clear when I speak. You have to be clear when you work in billing. If you get one number wrong, or explain a code poorly, the whole insurance claim gets kicked back. And you know how insurance companies are. They'll use any excuse to deny a claim. My cousin Brenda, she had this terrible time with her insurance last year when she needed that knee surgery. She tore her meniscus slipping on the ice in her driveway. It was one of those freak ice storms we got in February, remember? The whole city basically shut down for two days. The salt trucks didn't even make it to her neighborhood until the second afternoon. She was trying to walk down to get the mail because she was waiting for a birthday card from her son who lives out in Arizona. He moved out there for the dry heat, says it helps his allergies. But anyway, no, people don't tell me I'm hard to follow. I just tell things exactly how they happen.\n\nDoctor: Have you found yourself losing interest in seeing people or doing things you usually enjoy?\n\nPatient: Losing interest? No, I don't think so. I mean, I still like doing the things I usually do. Like my garden, I try to keep up with the flower beds out front. Mostly marigolds and some petunias. Though I will say, the slugs have been absolutely terrible this year. Have you noticed that? It's because we had such a wet spring. My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, he's lived next door for thirty years, he told me to put out little shallow dishes of beer to catch them. He says they're attracted to the yeast or something and they just crawl right in and drown. He buys the cheapest beer he can find at the discount liquor store over on 4th Street. The one next to that old dry cleaner that closed down? I used to take my winter coats there, but the last time I did, they lost the belt to my navy trench coat and refused to pay for it. The owner was this very stubborn man who insisted I brought it in without a belt. Why would I bring a trench coat in without a belt? It completely ruins the silhouette. But anyway, I still enjoy my garden and things like that. I just haven't been as social lately, but that's only because of everything going on with his family, you know? You have to be careful who you spend time with.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt that other people could read your thoughts?\n\nPatient: Read my thoughts? No, I don't think anyone can do that. He used to make me watch them with him when we first got married. We had this huge, heavy tube TV back then, the kind that took two people just to lift it onto the stand. The picture quality was terrible compared to what we have now, but we didn't know any better. We'd rent VHS tapes from Blockbuster on Friday nights. Remember Blockbuster? It's such a shame they all closed down. I used to love walking down the aisles, looking at all the covers. The smell of the popcorn they sold by the register... I bought a box of microwave popcorn last week, the extra butter kind, but it just doesn't taste the same. I think they changed the oil they use or something. The bag says \"new and improved flavor,\" but whenever a company says that, it usually just means they found a cheaper way to make it. It's like the brand of coffee I used to buy for the office breakroom. One day the packaging changed, and suddenly it tasted like burnt toast. I had to switch us to a different brand, which caused a whole fuss with the accounting department because it cost fifty cents more a can. But anyway, no, nobody can read my thoughts. I just keep them to myself, especially with everything his family is doing. You have to keep your thoughts private these days.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe your husband’s family has any special powers or unusual ways of controlling events that other people wouldn’t normally be able to do?\n\nPatient: Special powers? No, no, they don't have magic powers or anything like that. That's ridiculous. They're just very... manipulative. They know how to pull strings. Speaking of pulling strings, did you know I used to knit? I made this beautiful cable-knit sweater for my husband for our fifth anniversary. It took me months. He was always making excuses, saying the pipes were too old. But anyway, no, I've never been the suspicious type. I always try to see the good in people, until they give me a reason not to. It's just that now, with his family, they've given me plenty of reasons. But before that? No, I never thought people were out to get me.\n\nDoctor: Have you been convinced that your husband’s family is doing this for more than one month?\n\nPatient: Oh, definitely more than a month. I wore them until the knees completely wore out. You just can't find good corduroy anymore. Everything now is that thin, stretchy material that loses its shape after one wash. You really have to make sure you get up and stretch, otherwise your lower back just completely locks up. My sister-in-law, the one who married my brother David, she bought me one of those ergonomic cushions for my desk chair last Christmas. It’s got this memory foam in it that's supposed to mold to your shape. She got it off one of those home shopping channels, I think. She watches QVC all day long, buying the most ridiculous things. Last month she bought this set of copper pots that she swore were non-stick, but the very first time she tried to make scrambled eggs, they stuck right to the bottom. He built his own computer in his bedroom from parts he ordered online. It took up his whole desk, and it had these glowing blue lights inside the case. His mother was furious because he spent his entire summer job savings on it instead of saving for a car. My cousin Brenda, she had this terrible time with her insurance last year when she needed that knee surgery. She tore her meniscus slipping on the ice in her driveway. The one next to that old dry cleaner that closed down? I used to take my winter coats there, but the last time I did, they lost the belt to my navy trench coat and refused to pay for it. It's like the brand of coffee I used to buy for the office breakroom. One day the packaging changed, and suddenly it tasted like burnt toast. The water in our breakroom sink was always lukewarm, never hot enough to really get things clean, which I always thought was a health hazard. He was always making excuses, saying the pipes were too old. But anyway, no, I've never been the suspicious type. I always try to see the good in people, until they give me a reason not to. But anyway, no, people don't tell me I'm hard to follow. I just tell things exactly how they happen.\n\nDoctor: Have you found yourself losing interest in seeing people or doing things you usually enjoy?\n\nPatient: Losing interest? No, I don't think so. I mean, I still like doing the things I usually do. Like my garden, I try to keep up with the flower beds out front. Mostly marigolds and some petunias. Though I will say, the slugs have been absolutely terrible this year. Have you noticed that? It's because we had such a wet spring. My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, he's lived next door for thirty years, he told me to put out little shallow dishes of beer to catch them. He says they're attracted to the yeast or something and they just crawl right in and drown. He buys the cheapest beer he can find at the discount liquor store over on 4th Street. The one next to that old dry cleaner that closed down? I used to take my winter coats there, but the last time I did, they lost the belt to my navy trench coat and refused to pay for it. The owner was this very stubborn man who insisted I brought it in without a belt. Why would I bring a trench coat in without a belt? It completely ruins the silhouette. But anyway, I still enjoy my garden and things like that. I just haven't been as social lately, but that's only because of everything going on with his family, you know? He used to make me watch them with him when we first got married. We had this huge, heavy tube TV back then, the kind that took two people just to lift it onto the stand. The picture quality was terrible compared to what we have now, but we didn't know any better. We'd rent VHS tapes from Blockbuster on Friday nights. Remember Blockbuster? It's such a shame they all closed down. I used to love walking down the aisles, looking at all the covers. The smell of the popcorn they sold by the register... I bought a box of microwave popcorn last week, the extra butter kind, but it just doesn't taste the same. I think they changed the oil they use or something. The bag says \"new and improved flavor,\" but whenever a company says that, it usually just means they found a cheaper way to make it. It's like the brand of coffee I used to buy for the office breakroom. One day the packaging changed, and suddenly it tasted like burnt toast. I had to switch us to a different brand, which caused a whole fuss with the accounting department because it cost fifty cents more a can. But anyway, no, nobody can read my thoughts. I just keep them to myself, especially with everything his family is doing. You have to keep your thoughts private these days.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe your husband’s family has any special powers or unusual ways of controlling events that other people wouldn’t normally be able to do?\n\nPatient: Special powers? No, no, they don't have magic powers or anything like that. That's ridiculous. They're just very... manipulative. They know how to pull strings. Speaking of pulling strings, did you know I used to knit? I made this beautiful cable-knit sweater for my husband for our fifth anniversary. It took me months. I had to special order the yarn from a little shop up in Maine because I wanted this specific heather gray color. The woman who ran the shop, Mrs. Higgins, she was so sweet. She used to send a little handwritten note with every order and a complimentary stitch marker. They were always shaped like little sheep. I had quite a collection of them by the time she retired and closed the shop. It's so hard to find good quality wool these days without spending a fortune. Everything in the craft stores now is acrylic. It just doesn't breathe the same way, you know? You put on an acrylic sweater and five minutes later you're sweating, but you're still cold. It makes no sense. I tried to explain that to my sister when she started making baby blankets, but she just wanted something you could throw in the washer. But no, his family doesn't have special powers. He was always making excuses, saying the pipes were too old. But anyway, no, I've never been the suspicious type. I always try to see the good in people, until they give me a reason not to. It was slow, sure, but at least I knew how to fix it when it froze. You just had to hit Control, Alt, Delete, and wait for the little hourglass icon to go away. He says they're attracted to the yeast or something and they just crawl right in and drown. He buys the cheapest beer he can find at the discount liquor store over on 4th Street. The one next to that old dry cleaner that closed down? I used to take my winter coats there, but the last time I did, they lost the belt to my navy trench coat and refused to pay for it. The owner was this very stubborn man who insisted I brought it in without a belt. Why would I bring a trench coat in without a belt? It completely ruins the silhouette. But anyway, I still enjoy my garden and things like that. I just haven't been as social lately, but that's only because of everything going on with his family, you know? That sounds like something out of a science fiction movie. My husband loves those kinds of movies, the ones with aliens and mind readers and spaceships. He used to make me watch them with him when we first got married. We had this huge, heavy tube TV back then, the kind that took two people just to lift it onto the stand. The picture quality was terrible compared to what we have now, but we didn't know any better. We'd rent VHS tapes from Blockbuster on Friday nights. Remember Blockbuster? It's such a shame they all closed down. I used to love walking down the aisles, looking at all the covers. The smell of the popcorn they sold by the register... I bought a box of microwave popcorn last week, the extra butter kind, but it just doesn't taste the same. I think they changed the oil they use or something. The bag says \"new and improved flavor,\" but whenever a company says that, it usually just means they found a cheaper way to make it. It's like the brand of coffee I used to buy for the office breakroom. One day the packaging changed, and suddenly it tasted like burnt toast. I had to switch us to a different brand, which caused a whole fuss with the accounting department because it cost fifty cents more a can. But anyway, no, nobody can read my thoughts. I just keep them to myself, especially with everything his family is doing. You have to keep your thoughts private these days.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe your husband’s family has any special powers or unusual ways of controlling events that other people wouldn’t normally be able to do?\n\nPatient: Special powers? Speaking of pulling strings, did you know I used to knit? I made this beautiful cable-knit sweater for my husband for our fifth anniversary. It took me months. I had to special order the yarn from a little shop up in Maine because I wanted this specific heather gray color. The woman who ran the shop, Mrs. Higgins, she was so sweet. She used to send a little handwritten note with every order and a complimentary stitch marker. They were always shaped like little sheep. I had quite a collection of them by the time she retired and closed the shop. It's so hard to find good quality wool these days without spending a fortune. Everything in the craft stores now is acrylic. It just doesn't breathe the same way, you know? You put on an acrylic sweater and five minutes later you're sweating, but you're still cold. It makes no sense. I tried to explain that to my sister when she started making baby blankets, but she just wanted something you could throw in the washer. But no, his family doesn't have special powers. They're just very good at getting people to do what they want, normal things, just... twisted.\n\nDoctor: Before all of this started, have you generally tended to distrust other people and suspect they were trying to harm or deceive you?\n\nPatient: Distrust people? I mean, we're all adults, right? We had this one woman, Brenda, who started in the billing department a few years ago. She was always borrowing things. A pen here, a stapler there. One time she borrowed my favorite mug—it was this ceramic one I got on a trip to Sedona, painted with these beautiful little desert flowers. The glaze was so vibrant. Anyway, she borrowed it for her tea and then left it in the sink for three days. I finally had to wash it myself. The water in our breakroom sink was always lukewarm, never hot enough to really get things clean, which I always thought was a health hazard. He was always making excuses, saying the pipes were too old. But anyway, no, I've never been the suspicious type. I always try to see the good in people, until they give me a reason not to. I used to buy this special cream polish from a hardware store downtown, but they closed last year to make room for another one of those fancy coffee shops. I wore them until the knees completely wore out. You just can't find good corduroy anymore. Everything now is that thin, stretchy material that loses its shape after one wash. I bought a pair of pants last month from that department store at the mall—the one that used to be a Sears before they remodeled the whole wing. They put in a huge food court with this terrible lighting that gives you a headache if you sit there too long. I went there to get a pretzel, you know, the soft ones with the big grains of salt? But the line was a mile long, so I just left. Anyway, no, nobody is putting thoughts in my head. I know exactly what I'm doing and thinking. It's just his family that's the problem, not my own mind.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever feel that other people can hear your thoughts as you think them?\n\nPatient: Hear my thoughts? Oh, goodness, no. That sounds like something out of a science fiction movie. Like that one with the aliens that came down in those big silver saucers—what was it called? The Day the Earth Stood Still? My husband loved those old black-and-white movies. We used to stay up late on Friday nights watching them on this tiny little Zenith television we had in our first apartment. It had the rabbit ear antennas, and you had to wrap aluminum foil around the tips just to get a clear picture of channel 4. We lived right near the airport back then, so every time a plane flew over, the screen would get all fuzzy and the sound would buzz. I tried wedging a piece of cardboard in the side to stop the rattling, but it never really worked. The cardboard came from a box of oranges my uncle sent us from Florida. He had a grove down there, Valencia oranges, I think. They were the sweetest oranges I've ever tasted, so much juice you had to eat them over the sink. She swears by it, says it kept all the bugs off her prize-winning tomatoes last summer. She grows those big heirloom ones, the Cherokee Purples, I think they're called. They make the best BLT sandwiches if you toast the sourdough bread just right and use a really thick-cut bacon. My husband used to get this applewood smoked bacon from a butcher shop two towns over, but they closed down during the pandemic. Such a shame, it was a family-owned place, been there for three generations. The grandson was running it, but I guess he just couldn't keep the lights on...
